request.instructions: Speak Moroccan Darija with a natural Moroccan accent. Read only the supplied verb meaning 'to sign', exactly once, with no introduction, explanation, spelling, or translation. The input is a Latin phonetic rendering, not an English word. The characters ʿ and ʕ represent the voiced pharyngeal consonant ayn /ʕ/, ʾ and ʔ represent a glottal stop, ḥ and ħ represent a voiceless pharyngeal /ħ/, and q represents a uvular stop /q/, never the English name of a letter. A doubled q is a sustained consonant, not two words. Start with consonant w and a short unstressed vowel, preserve the doubled consonant and the final pharyngeal consonant. Output only the Moroccan word, without speaking the names of the symbols.
